---
title: "Areas, the Page List, and Sections"
---

These are three different lists. An Area chooses which Page List is open. The
Page List chooses a page. Sections are the headings of that page.

On desktop, Areas appear inline only when the site title, navigation and
Header controls fit. Otherwise the Areas button opens the same navigation
list in a panel. This adapts to long labels as well as narrow windows; no
consumer breakpoint setting is required. Pages still follows its own mobile
sidebar behavior. Very long site titles may be shortened visually, while
their full accessible name is retained.

| Role | Where it appears | What you put there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Areas | Header | One item per group of pages |
| Page List | Left column, titled Pages | The pages in the current Area |
| Sections | Right column, titled Sections | Nothing. Quarto lists the current page's headings |

```yaml
website:
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Guide
      - href: reference.qmd
        text: Reference
  sidebar:
    - title: Pages
      style: docked
      contents:
        - text: Overview
          href: index.qmd
        - text: Measure
          href: guide/measure.qmd
    - title: Pages
      style: docked
      contents:
        - text: Overview
          href: reference.qmd
        - text: API
          href: reference/api.qmd
```

Opening Guide shows the first Page List. Opening Reference shows the second.
`toc-title: Sections` and `toc-location: right` make the right column. A
heading belongs only in Sections, not in the Page List, and not as another Area.

Pages in one Area share a purpose. This Usage area is that kind of split: Add
Askr, this page, Versioning Docs, and Search are separate pages because each
one is a different job.

This gallery's Areas are Gallery, Components, Usage, Credits, and Long list.
The reading of that split is on the [Layout](../gallery/layout.qmd) page.
